purpose: Claim the benefit of the grace period under Section 31 — where a prior disclosure (display/use/publication/reading before a learned society) should not defeat novelty — selecting the applicable limb of Section 31 and submitting the required evidence.

fee.note: No explicit fee note appears on the face of Form 31; confirm against the current First Schedule for Rule 29A.

layout.notes: Two-column table with five numbered rows. Section 2 is a set of provision checkboxes (Section 31(a)-(d)); Section 3 provides, for each selected limb, a structured evidence block. Section 4 is a mandatory undertaking. Footer note: 'Select the options that are applicable.'

notes: Footer note: Select the options that are applicable.
The application must be made not later than 12 months from the date the invention entered the public domain; check the filing date against the earliest disclosure date.
Evidence may include an affidavit; where used, it must be signed by the applicant personally (not merely the agent).

Consent semantics differ per limb: sections 31(a) and 31(d) involve disclosure with consent or by the inventor, whereas section 31(c) specifically concerns use WITHOUT consent — these must not be blurred.
No explicit fee note appears on the face; confirm against the current First Schedule for Rule 29A.
